title: Yeah Nah Pasaran #299 w Leena van Deventer on GamerGate & the grievance economy : October 1, 2026
content:
This week on Yeah Nah Pasaran! we talk to Leena van Deventer [Bluesky]. Leena is a game developer, writer and researcher. Among her current interests is the concept of:

Hetconning (n.) — the deliberate retroactive straight-washing of history. Hetconned, the project, maps how the contemporary far-right market different post-truth fantasies to recruit and radicalise people into fighting for the Christo-nationalist project.

See also : Game Changers, Dan Golding and Leena Van Deventer (Affirm Press, 2016).

4.30pm, October 1, 2026 /// 855AM, digital, streaming, Community Radio Plus, podcats.

• This episode will be available as a podcast on Apple, Spotify and other platforms after broadcast. • We also have a Facebook page for the show, which you’re invited to ‘Like’ and to ‘Follow’, although because the anti-social platform is bloody awful, chances are you’ll never notice it.

title: Yeah Nah Pasaran #298 w Michael Bachelard on The Exclusive Brethren : September 17, 2026
content:
This week on Yeah Nah Pasaran! we talk to Michael Bachelard. Michael is a reporter for The Age and The Sydney Morning Herald and the author of Behind the Exclusive Brethren (Scribe, 2010), which details the church’s ‘origins in the United Kingdom in the nineteenth century, their fractious history, their extraordinary use of scripture to control members and dissidents, and their lucrative business and financial arrangements … a fascinating story of influence and power exercised across several continents.’

In ‘Tail, film, heckle’: Inside the Brethren’s secret election influence plot with the far-right by Sherryn Groch and Michael Bachelard (The Age, September 13, 2026), it was reported that ‘Leaked messages reveal the full story of how the Exclusive Brethren secretly recruited neo-Nazi associates to harass MPs at the election. As the church denies it, one elder confirms his involvement.’ Among the binfluencers named in the article are Laurence McIntyre, Chris de Bruyne (AKA Chriscoveries/Australian Firebrand), (Proud Boy) Harrison McLean, Barclay McGain (‘You’ve Done It Again’/CPAC Australia) and (‘That’s Freedom!’) Morgan C Jonas.

See also : ‘Assault on democracy’: Brethren leaders called to answer for far-right election plot, Michael Bachelard and Sherryn Groch, The Age, September 16, 2026 /// Who are the Brethren and what do they believe in?, Bernard Doherty, The Conversatio
